I have farmed these fields in Quzhou County for over fifty years. At seventy-six, I do not chase newfangled ideas. My bones know the rhythm of this plain: winter wheat in October, summer maize the moment the wheat comes off in June. I still hold 3.5 mu of good land—my sons took their shares years ago, but this patch is enough for my wife and me, with a little grain left over to sell.

This year I will stick to the wheat-maize double crop on the full 3.5 mu. It is the only system I trust. The agricultural station man told me last autumn that 20 kg of nitrogen per mu is the "scientific" rate for wheat, but I have learned that 22 kg is safer on my land; the soil here is decent but not rich, and I would rather waste a few yuan on extra urea than lose a hundred-jin yield to a pale crop. I will put down 100 jin of compound fertilizer as basal—that gives me about 8 kg of phosphorus and 6 kg of potassium per mu—and topdress with urea at green-up and jointing. For the maize, I will use a hybrid seed, Nongda 372 or whatever the seed shop has in stock this year, and spread 100 jin of compound fertilizer at planting, then see if it needs a side-dressing of urea at the big-trumpet stage. I figure about 18 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu for the corn.

Water is pumped from our tube-well, and electricity is not cheap, so I count every irrigation. The wheat will need four waters: the winter irrigation, the green-up water, one at jointing, and a final filling water if May turns dry. The maize is tougher; two good floods at jointing and filling will carry it through, assuming the summer rains do their job. For chemicals, I will spray the wheat three times—herbicide once, insecticide once, and a fungicide if the rust looks threatening. The maize gets three sprays too: herbicide at the three-leaf stage, then insecticide twice because the corn borer has been bad the last few years. I rotary-till before planting the wheat, but for the maize there is no time and no need; I will direct-seed into the wheat stubble like everyone else in the village.

I expect about 500 kg per mu from the wheat and 550 kg per mu from the maize. I used to get more when I was younger and had the strength to fuss over every row, but at my age steady and moderate is better than greedy and broken.
